record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Approachability of the radial lower bound
record.original_question: For m > 1 and r > 0, radial vector fields on punctured odd-dimensional spheres give a lower bound c(m,r) vol(S^{2m+1}) for the volume of smooth constant-length vector fields on S^{2m+1}, but this lower bound cannot be attained by a smooth vector field. Can c(m,r) vol(S^{2m+1}) nevertheless be approached as a limit of volumes of smooth vector fields of constant length r on S^{2m+1}?

evidence.quote: it’s not known if this value can be approached by the volume of smooth vector fields.

artifact.category_tag: Volume of vector fields on spheres
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m>1$ be an integer and let $S^{2m+1}\subset\mathbb{R}^{2m+2}$ denote the unit sphere with its round Riemannian metric. For a smooth vector field $V$ of constant length $r>0$ on $S^{2m+1}$, define its volume by
$$\mathrm{vol}(V)=\int_{S^{2m+1}}\sqrt{\det\big(I_{2m+1}+(\nabla V)^{T}(\nabla V)\big)}\,d\mathrm{vol},$$
where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection and $(\nabla V)$ is regarded as an endomorphism of $TS^{2m+1}$. 

Fix a point $p\in S^{2m+1}$ and consider the radial unit vector field on $S^{2m+1}\setminus\{\pm p\}$ given by the unit tangent field to minimizing geodesics issuing from $p$; rescaling by $r$ produces a constant-length-$r$ radial vector field whose (improper) volume equals $c(m,r)\,\mathrm{vol}(S^{2m+1})$ for an explicit constant $c(m,r)>0$. It is known that $c(m,r)\,\mathrm{vol}(S^{2m+1})$ is a lower bound for $\mathrm{vol}(V)$ over all smooth vector fields $V$ of constant length $r$ on $S^{2m+1}$, and that this bound is not attained by any such smooth vector field.

Question: Does there exist a sequence $\{V_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ of smooth vector fields of constant length $r$ on $S^{2m+1}$ such that
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{vol}(V_n)=c(m,r)\,\mathrm{vol}(S^{2m+1})\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the radial lower bound on odd-dimensional spheres of dimension greater than three can be approximated by volumes of smooth constant-length vector fields appears still open. Sources discussing the radial/north–south bound state that it is not attained by any smooth vector field, and approximations are known only for related single-singularity configurations on certain spheres; no source asserts a resolution in the general case $m>1$.

status_evidence.title: Poincaré index and the volume functional of unit vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: For dimension greater than three, the bound cannot be attained by any smooth vector field, but is the value of the volume of a family of vector fields with two singularities.
status_evidence.claim: The radial bound on higher-dimensional odd spheres is not realized by smooth vector fields.

status_evidence.title: Unit fields on punctured spheres
status_evidence.snippet: A family of unit vector fields with one singularity has been exhibited whose volume can be approximated by smooth unit vector fields.
status_evidence.claim: Approximation results exist for related singular configurations, but not directly for the two-singularity radial bound for general m>1.
